name: dsh-focus-free-shortcuts
description: Local runtime patch: make the right-Sidebar pane commands (fullscreen primary+alt+Enter, split primary+Backslash) and the double-Escape turn stop fire without first clicking into the pane or the composer. Both bundled commands resolve their owner from the keydown event target, and a keydown is dispatched to the focused element (or <body> when nothing is focused), so both silently decline until the user focuses the exact region: `pane.fullscreen.toggle` / `pane.split` call SidebarRight.focusedTarget(element) and return command.noFocus, while the fixed `response.stop` sequence requires its target inside [data-conversation-session] / [data-conversation-region]. This plugin opens its own fixed-input observer — the channel that runs for every keydown before configurable dispatch and can consume the press — and resolves the same owner without DOM focus: SidebarRight.commandTarget()'s active-dock-pane fallback for the pane commands, and the main-view Session for the stop (`sessions.list.byId[id].retainedBy.mainView > 0`, the same fact UiSession uses). It consumes a press only when it actually acts, and stands down whenever the bundled command owns that press, so exactly one owner remains per press. Nothing is registered in the shortcut catalog: no default bindings, no conflicts, no settings edits — and because the bridge follows the effective catalog row, a rebound, disabled, or absent bundled command is left alone. Pane keys are Web-runtime only: Desktop dispatches configurable bindings from its native bridge, where a DOM-side consume cannot suppress the bundled press.
